questions.prompt: Which publish model ships the .NET runtime with your app, so the target machine does not need .NET installed?
questions.explanation: In the publish types table, self-contained includes the runtime and the target machine does not need .NET, at the cost of a bigger size. Framework-dependent is smaller but needs .NET on the target.

questions.prompt: When do you need to run `dotnet restore` explicitly?
options: Before every `dotnet build`, because build never restores packages
Usually only in CI or when troubleshooting, because build, run, test and publish restore implicitly
Never, because the command was removed from the SDK
questions.explanation: The note says `dotnet build`, `dotnet run`, `dotnet test` and `dotnet publish` implicitly restore when necessary, and to use an explicit restore in CI or when troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: What does `dotnet add package Newtonsoft.Json` change in your project?
options: It edits the project file to include a `<PackageReference>`
It copies the package's source code into your project folder
It creates a new `.sln` file that lists the package
It publishes your project to NuGet.org
questions.explanation: Adding a package edits the project file to include a `<PackageReference>` and performs compatibility checks.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the industry CI/CD publish flow in order.
questions.explanation: The note's CI/CD flow goes from a push, through a CI build and `dotnet publish`, to an artifact that is deployed before the service is restarted.

options: A `publish/` folder ready to copy to a server
questions.explanation: `dotnet pack` creates a NuGet package from a project; the output is `.nupkg` files in `bin/Release`.

source.section: Create a package from a project

questions.prompt: On .NET 10 and later, how do you run a single `program.cs` file without creating a project?
questions.explanation: The note says `csc` and `mono` belong to the .NET Framework / Mono toolchain; on .NET 10 and later you use `dotnet run program.cs`.
